# dsh-memory-studio

A visual memory manager for DeepSeek Harness: local JSON stores, five views over
what it remembers,

and twelve tools an agent can call — with no server and no
API key.
Everything is local. No API key, no server, no dependency to install.
## What it gives you
It reaches you three ways, all pointing at the same screen:

- a **conversation tab** next to Chat / Trajectory;
- a **`main` panel** (`key: memory-studio`) that

fills the conversation area;
- a **row in the left rail** (`sidebar.panellist`), whose click select

s that panel —
this is the only destination a sidebar row can open, since a row cannot open a tab.
The screen has five sections:
| Section | What it is |
| **记忆** | Every durable note about the work: search, filter by kind and tag, edit, pin, archive, de

lete, 28-day heat strip. Matches show the sentence that hit. |
| **目录** | The same items as a tree —

按主题 (tag clusters → kind → memory) or 按会话 (session → turn → memory). Click a leaf to open it. |
| *
*我** | The profile — who you are, kept *apart* from work memories: identity fields plus facets under
identity / work / tooling / preference / constraint / goal / style, as cards or as a 类别 → 标签 → face

t tree. |
| **关系** | A force-directed graph of how memories relate: explicit links, shared tags, lex
ical overlap, same kind, same session, close in time. Drag, pan, zoom, click a node to see why it is

connected. |
| **待审** | Proposals the capture engine was not confident enough to save on its own, e
ach with the rule, the sentence and the confidence that produced it. Accept or dismiss in one click.
h with the rule, the sentence and the confidence that produced it. Accept or dismiss in one click. |
## Capture: what gets remembered, and what does not

When a session ends (or a turn stops and then goes quiet for `debounceMs`), the
engine reads the con

versation and applies a rule table in `lib/policy.js`.
Nothing is sent to a model — every candidate
cites the rule and the sentence.
**Never remembered** (dropped with a reason you can see in the report):

- confirmations — `好`, `ok`, `谢谢`, `收到` …
- log lines — `WARN …`, timestamps, stack-trace frames
- c

ode — `=>`, `const`, JSX, JSON fragments
- questions — a question asks for information, it does not

state a fact
- **everything the agent said** — capture reads only your side of the
conversation. Pro

se that merely sounds like a rule (`我们决定采用…`, written by
the agent) is still dropped, because a memo

ry should cite something *you*
said. When the agent genuinely wants a note kept, it calls `memory_wr

ite`
deliberately instead of hoping the classifier notices.
- imperative requests — `帮我做一个…`, `给我加个按

钮` (a task for this session,
not a fact about you; a standing rule like `以后都…` still counts as a pre

these arrive in the user role but are not things you said
- duplicates and things already known (fuz

zy match against memories + profile)
- anything without a matching rule

**Remembered**, with a weight per rule: identity and role (profile), work and
tooling context (profi

le), preferences, constraints, goals, decisions, todos,
insights, and plain facts worth keeping.

Confidence decides the destination: `autoSaveMemory` 0.80 and
`autoSaveProfile` 0.85 go straight in;

anything lower waits in **待审**. A
user's own words outrank the agent's summary of them (+0.06 / −0.

thing lower waits in **待审**. A
user's own words outrank the agent's summary of them (+0.06 / −0.18).

The profile can be injected at the start of a session as one short paragraph, so
you do not repeat y
ourself — toggle it in **我 → 自动沉淀**.
## Recall: pull, not push

Nothing is injected into a session — no profile paragraph at start, no hidden
system message. A memo

ry that sits in every prompt costs tokens on every turn
whether it is relevant or not, so recall is
driven by the assistant instead:

- `memory_brief` — one small digest (profile in a line or two, titles of pinned
and recent memories,

≤1.2k chars). Called once when a task depends on who the
user is or what was decided earlier.
- `me

mory_search` — hybrid recall of the long tail, with tags and kind filters.
- `profile_read` — the fu
ll portrait, only when the answer should be tailored.

The tool descriptions carry the rule: recall when the user refers to an earlier
session, a past deci

sion or a standing rule, or before asking something they may
already have answered. Skipping a recal
l is cheap; injecting everything is not.
## Retrieval: how a query is ranked

`memory_search` and the search box share one scorer in `lib/retrieval.js`, so the
assistant and the
page never disagree about what "relevant" means:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The embedding is local and dependency-free: tokens are Latin words plus CJK
uni/bi-grams, signed-has

hed into 384 dimensions, weighted by `(1 + log tf) · idf`
with title and tags up-weighted. It is not

a neural model — but it keeps the
store offline and deterministic (no model download, no API key),

while a
paraphrase like `导出成 md` still reaches a memory that says
`加一个导出按钮，把记忆导出成 Markdown`. BM25 ca

rries the precise half: two
memories that share the word `记忆` are ordered by how heavily each one le

ans on
it, not by string length. After ranking, the top hits widen one hop through the
graph, so a c
lose neighbour of a strong hit is not left behind.

Every result carries its score, and `GET /search` returns the breakdown
(`total`, `vector`, `lexical
`, `exact`, `prior`) so the UI can show why something ranked.
## Parent and child: small-to-big retrieval

A memory is the **parent**: the whole note is what the assistant needs once a
match is confirmed. Bu

t a three-paragraph note matched through one sentence
should not be scored by averaging over paragra

phs it has nothing to do with —
a long note loses to a short one on the same topic simply by being l

ong. So the
index is built on **children**: `content` is split into sentence-level chunks of
at most
180 characters (`CHUNK_CHARS`), and each chunk is scored on its own.

- `buildIndex()` returns `docs` (one per chunk, id `mem_x#0`, `mem_x#1`, …) and
`byItem` (parent id

→ its chunk ids). The parent's score is its **best**
chunk, plus a small coverage bonus (`min(0.06,

0.03 · (matches - 1))`) so a
